description:
Spike to de-risk the F# integration before scaffolding code.

Goals
1. Build a minimal F# console app that references `FSharp.Compiler.Service` (FCS).
2. Parse a representative F# file (modules, records, `let` bindings, `match`, async, computation expressions, type providers skipped) via `FSharp.Compiler.SourceCodeServices.FSharpChecker.ParseFile`.
3. Walk the resulting `FSharpAst` and confirm we can reach every node type the mapper will need: `SynModuleDecl`, `SynBinding`, `SynPat`, `SynExpr`, `SynType`.
4. Decide wire format. Two candidates:
   - **XML** — matches what `catseye_ast/tree_sitter_xml.ml` already consumes from tree-sitter. Lowest friction.
   - **JSON** — more typed, but requires a JSON parser in catseye_ast (we don't have one today) or a S-expression bridge.
   - Default: **XML**. Document the decision in a comment in `fsharp-extractor/Program.fs` so the mapper can rely on it.
5. Capture one concrete example file + the exact XML the extractor should emit, checked into `tests/fixtures/fsharp/spike-output.xml`. The mapper ticket references this fixture.

Acceptance
- `fsharp-extractor` compiles against FCS in a scratch directory.
- A short README note lives in the spike ticket describing the chosen wire format with one example.
- Decision recorded as a `bw comment catseye-9mh "..."` so the parent epic has a permanent breadcrumb.

Worktree: `catseye-9mh.1/fcs-spike` (epic-id + child ordinal).
title: FCS spike: confirm AST extraction + decide wire format
